first_impression.reaction: The intro is a bit scene-setty, but the second paragraph tells me exactly what's covered, so fine. The takeaways have a Smartraveller line in them, which told me this isn't just a mood board. I went to the FAQ first: short, plain answers, nobody pretending there's one right way. Then the Australia section and the venue questions, then I skimmed the customs.

journey.quote: Two families meet, ask, answer, present gifts and settle a list, and only then does the public celebration arrive, with its matching fabric, its music and a dance floor that fills fast.
journey.reaction: A bit of colour to open with. I skimmed past it. Not a problem, just not what I'm here for.

journey.quote: Smartraveller advises Australians to reconsider travel to Nigeria, so many diaspora couples bring these customs to a wedding in Australia or at another destination.
journey.reaction: Good. It says the awkward thing up front instead of selling me a Lagos trip. I'll check it on Smartraveller myself.

journey.section: What a traditional Nigerian wedding looks like today
journey.quote: Customs differ between Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa-Fulani families, and from one family and faith to the next.
journey.reaction: Right. No packaged 'authentic Nigerian wedding' to upsell me on. My partner's family will decide this, not a planner.

journey.section: 7. The bride price and the family list
journey.quote: Every family's list is its own, so settle it well ahead of the day.
journey.reaction: Fair. No numbers, which is right for something the families agree between themselves. I'd be wary of anyone who put a price on it.

journey.section: Travel to Nigeria for family: what Smartraveller says
journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Reconsider your need to travel" to Nigeria overall, including Abuja, and "Do not travel" to 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory outside Abuja.
journey.reaction: Dated, specific, quoted word for word, and it gives the number of states. That's the level of detail I want before I plan anyone's travel.

journey.quote: Aṣọ-òkè is hand-woven in narrow strips, and one workshop in Ilorin takes around 24 hours over a week to weave enough for a single jacket.
journey.reaction: A real lead time with a real place. Tells me to order early instead of just saying 'plan ahead'. Useful.

journey.section: Timing the traditional and white weddings
journey.quote: An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.
journey.reaction: That's the catch, said plainly, with 'in most cases' rather than a blanket promise. And it sends me to a lawyer, not to them. Good.

journey.section: Music, the alaga or MC and room for spraying
journey.quote: For an Igbo ceremony, is there a clear path through the guests for the bride's search, and can you bring in or serve palm wine, with what corkage?
journey.reaction: Corkage. Someone has actually thought about where venues sting you. Same with the noise limit and who keeps the cash safe during spraying. This is the most useful part of the page for me.

journey.section: Music, the alaga or MC and room for spraying
journey.quote: They work in your time zone and quote in AUD, the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing before any work begins is the right thing to say, and they're clear the nikah, church and legal steps stay with us. Still nothing on whether they take a cut from the venue or the band.

journey.section: Planning your Nigerian wedding with us
journey.quote: When you are ready to talk through dates, places or a wedding at home, tell us your date, your guest list and the feeling you want. Nothing is too early or too vague.
journey.reaction: 'The feeling you want' is soft. Tell me what the first call covers and whether it costs anything and I'm more likely to book it.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues, bands, caterers and other vendors?
What does the Wedded Advisor fee cover and how is it calculated?
Is the first conversation with a Wedded Advisor free, and what does it cover?
Have they planned a Nigerian or Nigerian-Australian wedding, and is there a real example with the actual budget?
Can they help source aso ebi or recommend tailors, or is that entirely on the families?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Nigerian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Clickbait headline, and the article is better than it. Title was set by the person, so noted only.

turn_offs_found.quote: Nothing is too early or too vague.
turn_offs_found.why: Reads like a sales line. I'd rather know what happens next. Minor.

would_share_with: My partner, for the venue questions, the corkage and noise limit points and the Smartraveller section
Her parents, to settle which stages and customs the family keeps and who chooses the aso ebi

cta_reaction.quote: They work in your time zone and quote in AUD, the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the useful stuff, not before, and the written fee line is what I look for. I'd still go hunting for a fees or commissions page before handing over my details.

top_3_changes: In the closing section, swap 'the feeling you want' and 'Nothing is too early or too vague' for what the first call covers and whether it's free.
Say, even in one line, whether the Wedded Advisor takes commissions or mark-ups from suppliers (business detail deferred, so nice-to-have).
Optionally trim the scene-setting in the opening sentence so the scope paragraph comes sooner. Minor.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for dates, downsides, fee model, commissions
No invented brand facts; missing fee, commission and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Title (person-set) and deferred business details not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or documentation lines, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: Is a fees or how-we-charge page available to link from the bridge CTA? Business details are deferred, so treat as nice-to-have.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'nigerian wedding traditions', implying his partner's family is Nigerian or Nigerian-Australian; relevance scored on that basis.
No prices on the page is the house standard and not penalised.
